text:
alex: Quick thought — we should consider a fast/slow query split for Console dashboards. Fastpath serves precomputed tiles + permissive cached RBAC check, slowpath does full authz pushdown and on-the-fly joins. Trying to capture tradeoffs before an RFC.
priya: Curious — what's the safety model on the fastpath? we can’t leak rows. :thinking:
alex: Agree. Proposal: fastpath only returns aggregated tiles (no raw rows) and uses token-scoped view: short-lived signed tokens that encode allowed tenant scopes. If token mismatch -> fallback to slowpath.
sam: From perf tests on staging, ~62% of dashboard hits are to the same 2–3 tiles. If fastpath hits those, p50 drops ~35-50ms. Worth exploring.
miguel: Invalidation is the blocker. Role/permission changes need quick eviction. Suggest event-driven invalidation: when IAM changes, publish tile keys to redis invalidation stream + short TTL (30s) for safety.
tanya: Alternative: push auth filters into the query planner (authz pushdown) so we avoid dual codepaths. Pros: single codegen path, no tile duplication. Cons: higher tail latency and more DB load for common tails.
priya: If we do fastpath, we need a deterministic acceptance test: tile must be aggregative-only, and token must assert a superset of permissions required by the tile filter. Otherwise go slow.
sam: Ops notes — metrics to add: fastpath_hit_rate, fastpath_evict_rate, token_misassoc_count, slowpath_latency_95. Also need circuit breaker when authz service unstable.
alex: Example config sketch:
```yaml
console:
  fastpath:
    enabled: true
    ttl: 30s
    max_cached_tiles_per_route: 200
    require_signed_tokens: true
```
miguel: For invalidation stream we can reuse existing infra: pubsub -> tile-invalidator consumers on all console nodes. Prevents thundering herd by batching invalidations for 200ms.
tanya: One more tradeoff — duplication of cache invalidation vs query planner complexity. Which team owns long-term maintenance? If product expects new RBAC features frequently, maintenance cost leans toward pushdown.
priya: Security asks: add explicit acceptance test and automated fuzzing to ensure no tile leaks across scopes. Also require audit logs whenever fastpath returns >0 rows for a tenant.
infra-bot: scheduled: perf/load test job console-fastpath-a11y will run Wed 03:00 UTC — results posted in #eng-releases. :white_check_mark:
sam: Next steps: prototype fastpath with strict acceptance (aggregates-only + signed tokens), run load tests, compare cost and tail latency vs pushdown. If prototype looks good, RFC + feature-flag rollout.
alex: Sounds good. Assigning follow-ups: @priya security acceptance, @miguel invalidation plumbing, @sam perf tests, @tanya cost/maintenance analysis. Will write short RFC draft after perf run. :thumbsup:
